data.turoyo: Fṣiḥ u ḥmoro, nʕəlle u ḥmoro w mʕarṭazle w rahəṭ.
data.translation: Da freute sich der Esel, schrie Tor Geilheit, schlug mit den Hinterbeinen aus und lief davon;

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; overt zero-marked donkey subject. Keep the edition's Tor typo and motive wording.

data.turoyo: Nʕəlli w rahəṭno, nafəl u taʕlo mə ḥaṣi.
data.translation: ich jauchzte laut auf und lief schnell weiter. Da fiel der Fuchs von meinem Rücken herunter

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; first-person l-series braying form in the donkey's retelling.

data.turoyo: Azze u dewo, mədle lu ḥmoro, nʕəlle lu ḥmoro, kle maṣro u ḥmoro.
data.translation: Da ging der Wolf hin und packte den Esel; dieser aber schrie auf; denn er war angebunden.

rationale: Fills Preterit cell to five; l-marked sound-emitter contrasts with zero-marked donkey at PrS 66/19.

data.turoyo: Məḏyaḏ kula nʕərla aʕle, nʕərla aʕle. Ġalabe ṭʕənla ġame. Ġalabe, ġalabe, səmme aʕle ḥəzniye.
data.translation: All Midyat cried out over him, cried out over him. It bore great sorrow. Very, very much, they mourned him.

rationale: The Preterit cell is full after round 1; select one unusually clear collective-human sound-source example with printed r-l preserved and an overt mourning context. Participant extension, not routine filler or a numbered lament sense; supplied machine English.

after: dröhnen; schreien, iahen (vom Esel; auch nachgeahmt);
rationale: The entry already quotes imitation of donkey braying; independent donkey subjects confirm that dröhnen alone omits the attested animal sound. Preserve the sense number.

summary: All eight records fit inherited sense 1 once its animal-sound component is made explicit. No new numbered sense is needed.
nʕəlle/nʕəlli/nʕəlla have r assimilated before the l-series suffix. The braying form is not nʕl 'shoe', even in the shoeing tale.

Sound-emitter subjects may be zero-marked (PrS 66/19 u ḥmoro) or l-marked (PrS 72/65 lu ḥmoro; cave li mʕarṯo at PrS 41/61 and 45/53). These are intransitive emitters, not recipients or experiencer objects.
PrS 42/71 nʕar is a genuine second-person Imperativ already quoted incidentally in the inherited Preterit example. Cross-filing the form adds a box, not a new occurrence count.
Reader context for PrS 74/78 includes earlier verses. The supplied verse translation is a sentence tail, so it is not used as a new standalone quotation.
Both supplied tokens occur in one verse and have separate decisions, but one shared example suffices. The copy preserves the source repetition because it belongs to the same complete utterance.
Round 1 already filled the Preterit cell and clarified donkey sound. Jan adds a collective human participant and unassimilated nʕər-la spelling, rather than evidence for a new box.

Məḏyaḏ is the grammatical collective emitter; -la is the l-series verbal ending, while aʕle identifies the person mourned. Do not interpret -la as a recipient or emend nʕərla to the assimilated head form. Supplied machine English remains unchanged.
Confirm edition concordances between PrS 41/61,45/53,42/71 and inherited prs 114/28,130/28,119/10 before citation changes.
Check inherited nʕəlla i=mʕarṯo against the supplied li mʕarṯo: was the subject's l-marker lost in the glossary quotation, or is this a source-version difference?
Jan 1.45/1943: is nʕər aʕl- a conventional mourning construction, or an ordinary cry with a contextual target? Obtain another independent context before a lexical lament sense is proposed.
Confirm whether the unassimilated r-l spelling reflects speech or editorial convention; no distinct paradigm is inferred.

Məḏyaḏ kula denotes the town's people as a collective feminine sound-source. Repeated nʕərla aʕle is motivated by grief; ʕal marks the person cried over. Contextual mourning does not by itself establish a separate lament sense.
